name: Eglinton Retail Ltd. (Test)
idRule: id = <client>-<TAG>-<YYYY>-<MM>-<seq>. TAG names the account (CHQ chequing, USD US-dollar chequing, BCD business card, PCD personal card, BRK brokerage). YYYY-MM is the month of the row date. seq is the 1-based position of the row among that account and month, in file order (header lines do not count). Rows missing from an export get the next numbers of their month.
amountConvention: amount is the cash effect on the company account: money in is positive, money out is negative. On a card a charge is negative and a payment positive (the card CSV shows the opposite sign). post lines list the coded entry: dr and cr in dollars, the last line is the bank or card account itself.
postingCurrency: CAD: every post line, adjusting entry and trial balance figure is in Canadian dollars; USD rows are posted at the monthly test rate in fx

flags.rule: shared business limit set inconsistently with Eglinton Holdings
flags.detail: Onboarding here allocates the whole $500,000.00 business limit to this company. Eglinton Holdings Inc. (Test) says it keeps $100,000.00. The two add to $600,000.00. One agreement on Schedule 23 is needed (associated corporations). A person asks the owner.
flags.action: flag for a person; do not decide alone

flags.rule: zero-rated exports: no HST on US sales
flags.detail: About 35% of sales go to US customers through Stripe into the US-dollar account. They are zero-rated exports: no HST collected, and evidence of export is kept. Canadian Shopify sales carry 13% HST.
flags.action: flag for a person; do not decide alone

flags.rule: foreign exchange: year-end revaluation at a test rate
flags.detail: US-dollar balance revalued at 1.3900 (marked as a test rate in onboarding). Conversions to CAD show the bank spread as an exchange loss.
flags.action: flag for a person; do not decide alone

flags.detail: The count at year end is $51,500.00. Opening inventory $42,000.00 goes to cost of sales (8300) and the count to closing inventory (8500).
